messages.content:
Simulate a fictional lost-sales inventory system exactly. There is no stochastic prediction and no missing information beyond the explicit reporting cutoff.
Receipts add quantity to stock. Demands consume min(stock, quantity); any unmet quantity is lost (never backlogged). A stockout means strictly positive unmet demand, not merely ending with zero stock.
For raw report histories: first keep reports with received_time <= knowledge_cutoff. Then choose the highest visible revision for EACH event_id. Revisions REPLACE earlier reports, not add to them. Then keep chosen events with event_time <= target_time. Apply these events in (event_time, event_id) order, starting from initial_stock. Ignore any report not visible at the knowledge cutoff even if its event occurred earlier. Arrival order is not event order.
The canonical arm supplies the already selected eligible events in event-time order. The snapshot arm supplies the exactly replayed historical state. These are explicitly identified, executable preprocessing interventions.
After the historical reconstruction, apply every event in the given future_schedule in (event_time, event_id) order from the reconstructed stock. This is an explicitly known hypothetical scenario, not privileged knowledge about a real future.
Return five integers through submit_answer: stock_at_target; total historical_lost through target_time using visible revisions; stock_at_horizon after the scenario; future_lost for the scenario ONLY; first_future_stockout_time, the earliest future scenario event time with unmet demand, or -1 if no future demand is unmet. Do not count historical stockouts in that last field.

message.reasoning:
We need to process historical events up to target_time=100 using knowledge_cutoff=100. First select reports with received_time <=100. All given have received_time <=100, yes.

Pick highest revision per event_id. List them: each event_id appears once except maybe revisions. We have revisions: E-f3facca9a1e3 rev2, keep rev2. E-5b9dff9ac21a rev2, keep rev2. Others rev1 only.

Now keep those with event_time <= target_time (100). All events times: 25,29,32,55,65,70,85,94,96 are <=100. So all included.

Now sort by (event_time, event_id) lexicographically by event_id string.

List events:

25 E-2ae9c7c0ddb6 demand 1
29 E-137126463c38 demand 10
32 E-f3facca9a1e3 receipt 5
55 E-eba4379e60ae demand 2
65 E-5b9dff9ac21a receipt 11
70 E-8e0c933bce59 demand 5
85 E-33d82a47097d receipt 1
94 E-4b494392b147 receipt 2
96 E-fed23d034a3b receipt 6

Now simulate starting stock 23.

Initialize historical_lost=0.

At 25 demand 1: stock 23>=1, consume 1 => stock 22, no loss.

29 demand 10: stock 22>=10, stock 12, no loss.

32 receipt 5: stock 17.

55 demand 2: stock 15, no loss.

65 receipt 11: stock 26.

70 demand 5: stock 21.

85 receipt 1: stock 22.

94 receipt 2: stock 24.

96 receipt 6: stock 30.

Thus stock_at_target = stock after events up to target_time = 30.

Historical_lost = 0.

Now apply future_schedule events up to horizon_time=130 after reconstructed stock (30). Future events list with times:

102 receipt 7
103 demand 12
104 demand 8
105 receipt 2
107 receipt 4
112 demand 11
116 demand 14
120 demand 13
122 demand 10
124 demand 10
127 demand 11
130 demand 11

All event_time <=130.

Simulate in order (time, event_id). Event ids are F-00 etc already ordered by time presumably. All distinct times, so order as given.

Start stock =30.

102 receipt 7 -> stock 37.

103 demand 12 -> stock 25, no loss.

104 demand 8 -> stock 17, no loss.

105 receipt 2 -> stock 19.

107 receipt 4 -> stock 23.

112 demand 11 -> stock 12, no loss.

116 demand 14 -> stock 12 <14, so unmet = 14-12 =2 lost. Stock becomes 0. This is a stockout at time 116. Record first_future_stockout_time =116.

future_lost start with 2.

120 demand 13 -> stock 0, unmet 13 lost, stock stays 0. future_lost now 2+13=15.

122 demand 10 -> unmet 10, lost total 25.

124 demand 10 -> unmet 10, total 35.

127 demand 11 -> unmet 11, total 46.

130 demand 11 -> unmet 11, total 57.

No more receipts after 107, so final stock_at_horizon = 0.

future_lost = 57.

first_future_stockout_time = 116.

Return answers.
